title: Ticks in Poland — what you need to know
question: Are ticks dangerous in Poland and what should I do if I get bitten?
short_answer: Yes. Ticks in Poland can carry Lyme disease (borelioza) and tick-borne encephalitis (TBE). Season runs April–October. Remove immediately and see a doctor.
conditions: Tick season: April to October, peak in May–June and August–September
High-risk areas: forests, parks, meadows, tall grass
After outdoor activity: check your whole body, especially armpits, groin, neck, behind knees
Remove tick with tweezers: grab close to skin, pull straight out — do not twist or crush
Clean the bite site with antiseptic
Mark the date of the bite and monitor for 30 days
exceptions: Red expanding rash (rumień wędrujący) around the bite = likely Lyme disease — see a doctor immediately
Flu-like symptoms within days of a bite (fever, headache, fatigue) — see a doctor
TBE vaccine is available in Poland and recommended for people spending time in forests
